newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CSR, Mackay not in merger talks-ACCC.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CSR, Mackay not in merger talks-ACCC.

text.p: Building materials and sugar group CSR Ltd and fellow sugar refiner the Mackay Sugar Cooperative Association were not in merger talks, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) said on Friday.
ACCC Chairman Allan Fels said players in the sugar industry were in discussions about how to rationalise away excess capacity and boost exports without harming local competition.
But these talks did not include the prospect of a CSR-Mackay merger, he said.
There has been regular market speculation recently about a merger.

"It's true that there's been some talks between us and people in the sugar industry about possible steps that could be taken to help rationalise the industry," Fels told reporters after a speech to company secretaries.
"But they're not talking about having a merger between CSR and Mackay," he said.
"The industry wants to boost exports without having severe anti-competitive effects," he said.
Fels said discussions were not advanced enough for specific proposals, but that the parties were considering some body to jointly promote and produce exports.
Earlier this month, Prime Minister John Howard criticised the country's anti-merger rules, saying they had prevented a sugar industry merger in 1993 that some experts had regarded as necessary.
In December 1993, the then Trade Practices Commission rejected a proposed merger between CSR, Mackay and British commodities house E D & F Man Group Plc.
The commission, now that ACCC, said at the time that economic gains from the merger would not offset the loss of competition that it would involve.
